description: A shared geochemical database of critical elements in ore samples from around the world. USGS Fact Sheet 2025-3002 (version 1.2, May 2025) says the Critical Minerals Mapping Initiative of the USGS, the Geological Survey of Canada and Geoscience Australia compiled more than 20,000 ore samples from more than 100 deposit types in 10 geological environments, with analyses of critical elements, so that users can see which deposit types host which critical minerals, and that the data are published by Geoscience Australia with a persistent identifier. The fact sheet and data are free. Coverage is global deposits. Caveats: sample density varies by country and deposit type, and the licence of the dataset is on the Geoscience Australia page, which was not readable from the cloud. For simulation it helps estimate where by-product critical minerals could come from, for supply diversification scenarios. A related catalogue record is the USGS critical mineral deposits of the United States.
